Cinnamon Star Cookies

Served at: Second Sunday of Advent

Makes about 30 cookiesPrep 20 minCook 15 min

Cinnamon Star Cookies, or Zimtsterne, are a traditional German Christmas treat especially popular during Advent. These delicate, spiced cookies are shaped like stars and topped with a sweet meringue glaze, symbolizing the festive spirit of the Second Sunday of Advent.

Ingredients

  • 3 large egg whites
  • 1 cup (200 g) granulated sugar
  • 2 1/2 cups (250 g) ground almonds
  • 1 tablespoon ground cinnamon
  • 1 teaspoon lemon juice
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • Powdered sugar for dusting

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 300°F (150°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. In a clean bowl, beat the egg whites until soft peaks form.
  3. Gradually add granulated sugar while continuing to beat until stiff, glossy peaks form.
  4. Reserve about one-third of the meringue for the topping and set aside.
  5. In a separate bowl, combine ground almonds, cinnamon, lemon juice, and vanilla extract.
  6. Gently fold the remaining meringue into the almond mixture until a sticky dough forms.
  7. Dust a clean surface with powdered sugar and roll out the dough to about 1/4 inch (6 mm) thickness.
  8. Cut out star shapes using a cookie cutter and place them on the prepared baking sheet.
  9. Spread the reserved meringue evenly over each star cookie.
  10. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until the meringue is set but not browned.
  11. Allow cookies to cool completely on the baking sheet before transferring to a wire rack.

Tips

  • Use fresh egg whites at room temperature for better meringue volume.
  • Store cookies in an airtight container to keep them crisp.
  • For a nut-free version, substitute ground almonds with finely ground hazelnuts or omit nuts and increase cinnamon slightly.
